name: Spotify Web
description: A full-stack music catalog and player — React front end, Express + MongoDB API, deployed end-to-end on Render.
heroAlt: Illustration of a man with headphones tending a garden bed, surrounded by music notes

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Solo developer — design, front end, back end, deploy

content.text: Spotify Web is a full-stack music catalog and player built end-to-end: a curated library of 20 Brazilian artists and 200 songs, browsable by artist or track, with a custom audio player for playback. What started as a front-end-only clone was rebuilt around a real Express and MongoDB API to practice shipping one complete slice — UI, API, database, and deployment — as a single working product.
Three core screens: browse artists, drill into an artist’s discography, and play a track with the custom audio player.

columns.alt: Home screen with the top artists and songs
columns.caption: Home — top artists & songs

columns.alt: Player screen with the track now playing
columns.caption: Player — now playing

content.text: One process serves both sides: Express exposes two read endpoints backed by MongoDB Atlas, then falls back to the compiled React build for every other route — so client-side routes survive a hard refresh.

content.alt: Architecture diagram: the browser loads the React build, which calls the Express API; Express reads the artists and songs collections from MongoDB Atlas and falls back to index.html for client-side routes

content.text: Two flat, denormalized MongoDB collections — no joins, no relations. The front end fetches both in full and does all filtering client-side.
The whole project — front end and back end — lives in one repo as two independent Node projects, orchestrated from a root package.json so a single build/start pair covers both.

columns.title: back-end
columns.code:
cd back-end
npm install
npm run dev
# http://localhost:3001

columns.title: front-end
columns.code:
cd front-end
npm install
npm run dev
# http://localhost:5173

items: Eager data loading: the whole artist and song catalog loads once at startup and is filtered in memory client-side — simple at 20 artists / 200 songs, a deliberate trade-off that would need pagination and search to scale further.
Custom audio player built directly on the `<audio>` element: play/pause, a polled progress bar, and next/previous that jumps to a random track by the same artist rather than a fixed queue.
Single Express service serves both the API and the compiled front end, so one Render deployment covers the whole stack instead of two.

content.text: The result is a working, publicly deployed app with a real catalog, artist and song detail pages, and a functioning custom player — plus a self-authored architecture doc that names its own gaps (no auth, no search, config that should move to environment variables) as concrete next steps rather than hiding them.

items: Pagination and search once the catalog stops being small enough to hold in memory
Loading and error states for the API calls
A real play queue instead of random shuffle
Config through environment variables instead of hardcoded values
